parameters.description:
`msg-to-mastodon` accepts an HTTP POST carrying the unified `msg` envelope (`title`, `body`, `type`, `format`), attaches the credentials in your stored secrets, and delivers the message to your Mastodon instance — so you run no messaging infrastructure of your own.

Delivery goes out through a native gateway transformation that posts straight to your own Mastodon instances — free, and driven entirely by the credentials you have stored. Paid variants ($0.001 / message) deliver to additional Mastodon instances bound per enrollment.

In your Mastodon account's Settings, open the Development tab and create a new Application — this is what will post on your behalf. Grant it at least the write:statuses scope (add write:media too if you plan to send attachments), then save. Reopen the application's configuration and copy its Access Token into MASTODON_TOKEN; only the access token is needed, not the key or secret shown alongside it.
